sections.h2: What kind of town is Southington, Connecticut?
sections.html:
Southington is a Hartford County town about 20 miles southwest of Hartford, and it is known as the Apple Valley. Wikipedia lists a 2020 census population of 43,501 across 36.6 square miles, with 17,149 households and 18,154 housing units.

The town includes three villages, Plantsville, Marion and Milldale, and each has its own post office and its own style of older housing. The town sits in a valley, with ridges on its east and west sides, and the Quinnipiac River crosses it.

Southington has a council-manager government with a nine-member Town Council. Voters also elect a Planning and Zoning Commission, Board of Education, Board of Finance, Water Commission and Town Clerk, so zoning and recording questions each have their own local office.

sections.h2: How did Southington grow, and why does it matter for older houses?
sections.html:
Southington was a farming settlement known as Panthorne in 1698, became a separate town in 1779, and turned into a manufacturing center in the early 1900s. Inventions credited to local shops include a cement that hardens under water and a carriage bolt cutting machine.

After Interstate 84 was built in the mid 1960s, the town became a bedroom community. Census counts went from 13,061 in 1950 to 22,797 in 1960 and 30,946 in 1970, then past 43,000 by 2010.

That timeline produces a mix of houses sellers should recognize:

  • Colonial and 19th-century houses near the town center and Plantsville, including the Capt. Josiah Cowles House (c. 1750).
  • Mid-century capes and ranches built during the 1950s and 1960s boom.
  • Later subdivisions that fill the valley and the lower slopes.

Southington also lists dozens of buildings on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Marion, Plantsville and Southington Center historic districts. Check with the town before you plan exterior changes to a house in one of those districts.

sections.html:
The town itself, a regional health system and a major bank lead the list. Wikipedia reproduces the table below from the town's 2019 annual financial report, so headcounts are older than other figures on this page.

Wikipedia also says about 28 percent of Southington workers are in manufacturing, mostly fabricated metals and aircraft parts. Plant closings and layoffs in those trades are one reason homeowners here sometimes need a faster sale than a listing can offer.

sections.h2: What weather and terrain should a Southington seller think about?
sections.html:
Southington has had a serious tornado. On May 24, 1962, a high-end F3 tornado damaged or destroyed many buildings in the area, leaving one person dead and 50 injured, according to Wikipedia's account of National Weather Service records.

Such storms are rare, but wind and tree damage to roofs is a more common issue. The town also sits at the base of the Metacomet Ridge, which includes Ragged Mountain and Short Mountain on the eastern edge, so some lots slope steeply.

  • Hillside parcels can mean retaining walls, drainage problems and long driveways, which buyers and appraisers look at closely.
  • The Quinnipiac River and its brooks put some low parcels near water, so ask your insurer about flood zone status.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit shape the market in Southington?
sections.html:
Southington is served by Interstate 84 at exits 28 through 32, Interstate 691 at exits 5 through 7, and Route 10, which runs through the town. Interstate 84 is also called the Yankee Expressway.

CTfastrak express buses run between Hartford and Waterbury with a free park-and-ride at South Main and Mulberry streets in Southington, and CT Transit began route 532 along Queen Street in 2024. Waterbury connects to Metro-North rail service.

The Farmington Canal Greenway runs through Plantsville, and the town is home to Lake Compounce, which dates to 1846, and Mount Southington ski area. If your house is close to the trail, the town center or these attractions, say so when you describe it.

sections.h2: What is the Ideal Forging site, and does it affect nearby sellers?
sections.html:
Ideal Forging was a factory in the town center that went bankrupt in 2001 and left its building vacant. A 2005 redevelopment plan stalled because decontaminating the soil was costly, and demolition began in October 2014.

As of 2023, preparations began for a new attempt at redevelopment, with soil cleanup subsidized by the EPA, the state and the town. For a seller near the center, the site is a reminder that former industrial land is a factor in buyer questions, so ask the town or the state environmental agency if you are unsure about a specific parcel.

sections.h2: What does the seller pay at closing on a Southington house?
sections.html:
Connecticut taxes the transfer itself. Under Section 12-494 of the statutes, a deed worth $2,000 or more carries a conveyance tax of 0.75 percent for the state plus 0.25 percent for the town, a combined one percent on most homes (Chapter 223).

On a $350,000 sale that is $3,500, and on $1.2 million it is $14,000, because the state portion rises to 1.25 percent on the slice above $800,000. Here is how the rules break down:

  • Residential price up to $800,000: 0.75 percent state, 0.25 percent town.
  • Residential price from $800,000 to $2.5 million: 1.25 percent state on that slice.
  • Above $2.5 million: 2.25 percent state on that slice.
  • Some conveyances are exempt, such as a principal residence given in lieu of foreclosure or a sale that does not cover the mortgages and priority tax liens.

The Department of Revenue Services requires the grantor to file Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded. Southington is town code 131 on the state's list, and the town clerk can tell you whether it accepts electronic filing through myCTREC (state instructions).

sections.h2: When are Southington property taxes due, and what happens if you are late?
sections.html:
Each Connecticut town decides whether to bill in one, two or four installments. State law only requires that the last installment be due at least 45 days before the fiscal year ends (Chapter 204).

An installment not paid by the first day of the following month is delinquent and carries 18 percent annual interest, with a $2 minimum unless the town waived it. Confirm the actual installment dates, mill rate and any sewer charges with the Southington Tax Collector and Assessor before you set a closing date, because tax proration is figured from those numbers.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Southington?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when time or condition matters more than the last dollar. Sellers with inherited houses, back taxes, failed inspections or a move already scheduled often pick it.

We buy houses in Southington as-is, and you can compare our offer to a listing price after subtracting repairs, showing time, the conveyance tax and carrying costs. If a listing wins for your house, that is fine too.

faqs.a: Yes. Southington is a Hartford County town in the Capitol Planning Region, about 20 miles southwest of Hartford, with 43,501 residents in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: What are the villages of Southington?
faqs.a: The town includes Plantsville, Marion and Milldale. Each has its own post office and its own older housing.

faqs.q: How much is the Connecticut conveyance tax on a Southington home sale?
faqs.a: On most homes it is one percent of the sale price, split 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town. A $350,000 sale would owe $3,500 under those rates.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Southington house with an unpaid tax bill?
faqs.a: Usually yes. The balance and interest are typically paid out of the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the tax collector for a payoff figure.
Interstate 84, Interstate 691 and Route 10 serve the town, and CTfastrak express buses stop at a park-and-ride at South Main and Mulberry streets.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix problems before a cash sale in Southington?
faqs.a: No. We buy as-is, and the cost of repairs is part of how we calculate the offer.
